- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- Underestimate during mean-reversion phases; adjust upward if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for 2–3 days.
- Lagged forecasts consistently underestimate; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for each day lagged beyond 10 days.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 2–3% to avoid overcorrection.
- Avoid overfitting to recent volatility; if 30-day history shows high variance, use 20-day rolling mean as baseline for adjustment.
